title: Native coefficient transport and sectionwise module presentation
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a scheme $T$ with its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $R_T$ be the finite-extension-valued coefficient ring sheaf for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed] and [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and $B_T$ the native locally finite-span coefficient ring in the native module heart [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. Define $\vartheta_T:R_T\cong B_T$ as the normalized coefficient realization of [lem-sf-locally-finite-coefficient-ring-realization], characterized on every finite-extension leg; retain its ring-morphism structure. Use the section-ring reconstruction and internal/sectionwise equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence] for $R_T$. Define $\operatorname{OrdMod}(T)$ as sectionwise module sheaves over this reconstructed ring sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Define the functor from native modules to $\operatorname{OrdMod}(T)$ by first forgetting scalar linearity to internal abelian-sheaf modules, then restricting the action along $\vartheta_T$, then applying that fixed sectionwise presentation. Thus the underlying abelian sheaf and restriction maps are retained, and $r\in R_T(V)$ acts by the original action of $\vartheta_T(r)$. These definitions do not assert constructibility or an equivalence theorem about this functor.
